relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - the page states an obligation ("we need to escape that by replacing it with") conditional on a situation (using % as a wildcard in a query), which is mustUseInsteadWhen's shape

notable_absence.finding: The page has no cross-references at all - no See Also section and no inline links. In particular it does not link to the named/positional parameter documentation in server/current/n1ql/n1ql-manage/query-settings.md, which is where the feature is actually specified and where the @-prefixed alternative syntax lives. The Capella corpus links this concept the other way round (cloud/guides/prep-statements.json records seeAlso -> n1ql:named-and-positional-parameters), so the link exists in one direction only.

version_finding:
1. INCOMPLETE SYNTAX COVERAGE RELATIVE TO THE SAME PRODUCT VERSION. Server 8.0 documents two placeholder prefixes for named parameters. server/current/n1ql/n1ql-manage/query-settings.md uses both in the same statement - "WHERE country = $country AND geo.alt > @altitude;" - but this example page shows only the $ form ($aval, $dval, $pattern) and never mentions @. The Capella page cloud/n1ql/n1ql-manage/query-settings.md carries the identical @altitude example, so this is not a Server/Capella divergence: it is an example page that has not been refreshed since the @ prefix was introduced. Since neither page states when @ became available, this is exactly the availableSince fact the registry has no way to record and the docs have no way to convey. Flagging for reconciliation: the @ prefix is a candidate for an availableSince relation once a version can be sourced, and this page is a candidate doc fix.

2. No version or edition gating on the page itself.
cross_component_finding:
DOCUMENTATION DEFECT: the parameter table misnames a parameter. The table lists the parameters as `statement`, `$aval` and `$davl`, but the statement in the same table row and the curl command below both use `$dval`:

  | $davl          | 13000                                                                                                   |

against

  & $aval="LAX" & $dval=13000' \

`$davl` is a transposition typo for `$dval`. A reader copying from the table would get error 1050 ("No statement or prepared value" family - unresolved named parameter), which is precisely the failure mode documented on this batch's exrequesterror.md. Worth fixing; the equivalent table on expositional.md ($1, $2) is correct, so this is isolated to exnamed.md.
